title: Importing Selected Names with from
learningObjectives: Explain from module import name and where it is useful in Python programs.
Choose correct Python syntax for from module import name.
Predict the result of representative PY16.4 operations.
Identify namespace, import and maintenance risks related to from module import name.

understand.concept: The `from module import name` form binds a selected member directly in the current namespace. It can make short examples concise, but it may hide where a name came from and can overwrite an existing local name. Use it selectively and avoid wildcard imports in application code.
understand.whyItMatters: Selective imports are useful when a file needs a small number of well-known names, while understanding their namespace effects prevents confusing collisions.
understand.analogy: A module is like a labelled toolbox: related tools are stored together and another program can request the tools it needs.
understand.analogyLimit: A real Python module also has import rules, namespaces, execution behaviour and caching that a physical toolbox does not represent.
understand.summary: Importing Selected Names with from teaches how Python organizes and reuses related code.

explain.narrative:
## Selective import
`from math import sqrt` makes `sqrt` available directly, so call `sqrt(49)` rather than `math.sqrt(49)`.

## Import several names
A comma-separated list can import several members from the same module. Each imported name is bound in the current namespace.

## Aliases and collisions
Use `from module import name as alias` when a shorter or clearer local name is needed. Be aware that a later assignment can replace an imported binding.

## Avoid star imports
`from module import *` makes namespace contents less predictable and is discouraged for normal application code. Prefer explicit names or a qualified module import.

examples.title: Import one selected function
examples.explanation: The selected function is bound directly in the current namespace.

examples.title: Import two constants
examples.code:
from math import pi, tau
print(round(pi, 3))
print(round(tau, 3))
examples.explanation: Several selected names can be imported in one statement.

examples.title: Use an imported name with a comprehension
examples.code:
from statistics import mean
scores = [70, 80, 90]
print(mean(scores))
examples.explanation: The imported function can be called directly.

examples.title: Alias a selected import
examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal as D
price = D('12.50')
print(price * 2)
examples.explanation: The alias D is a local name for Decimal.

examples.title: Understand local name replacement
examples.code:
from math import pi
print(round(pi, 2))
pi = 3
print(pi)
examples.explanation: An imported name is an ordinary local binding and can later be reassigned.
